newsitem.title: USA: Digital seen returning to revenue growth.
newsitem.headline: Digital seen returning to revenue growth.

text.p: Digital Equipment Corp appears set for a recovery from heavy price cuts in January and for a return to revenue growth in the first quarter, analysts said.
Chief Financial Officer Vincent Mullarkey told reporters Thursday that Digital should see growth in overall revenues and in Alpha sales as soon as the current first quarter.
"All in all, Alpha isn't doing as badly as some people might think," said Terry Shannon, publisher of the independent newsletter "Shannon Knows DEC."
Shannon said unit sales of Alpha computer systems have actually been growing strongly, but the January price cuts hurt margins, accounting for the drop in year-over-year revenues from the products.
"They're out there selling boxes, but they're not making as much because of the mother of all price cuts in January," he said. "That doesn't translate into revenue growth."

Richard Chu, an analyst with Cowen Corp, said that based on the company's fourth quarter results released Thursday, he raised his 1998 earnings estimates and his recommendation on the stock to a strong buy from neutral.

Chu said he raised his fiscal 1998 earnings estimates to $2.75 per share from $2.45 per share. Digital reported earnings per share for the year ended June 28 of $0.68 on Thursday. Digital shares, which were trading at 41-3/4 in mid-afternoon on Thursday, could climb to the mid-50s, he said.
"We definitely like the results," he said. "I think one can attach a higher level of confidence to those numbers. They've addressed some of the problem spots."
One problem spot Digital recently addressed was its sales and marketing effort.

"It's just hard to get excited about this as a technology stock," said one analyst, who declined to be named. "It looks like a value stock because of its low market cap to revenue. Just being cheap isn't good."
"The growth rate of Alpha is lackluster; the growth rate of PCs isn't really at the industry rate," he added.
Digital announced in April a reorganization in that areas and named Bruce Claflin to head sales and marketing.

"The Quarter Four results indicate there was no disruption associated with this reorganization," Shannon said. "I think the company looks a lot better today than most people would have guessed one year ago."
For the fourth quarter the year before, Digital reported a net loss of $433 million, which included a restructuring charge of $492 million.
But at least one analyst said that while Digital may look better, its prospects for strong growth are bleak.
